note: GLOBALCIT's Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (EUI, 2025), coding the law in force on 1 January 2024 (A06a EGY 4(5); A06b EGY 4(5); L05 EGY 10): ordinary naturalisation after 10 years' residence; no renunciation of other citizenships required; a citizen loses the citizenship on voluntarily taking another (with exceptions). Reforms after that date are checked in the file's later sources, where a later source is given. Citizenship at birth is read from the same dataset's 2024 coding of modes A01a (descent, born in country: Generally applicable provision), A01b (descent, born abroad: Generally applicable provision), A02a (birth in country: No provision) and A02b (birth in country to a parent born there: No provision), as its codebook (RSC/GLOBALCIT 2025/01, sections 3.2.1a to 3.2.2b) defines them: not by birth in the territory alone (provisions for foundlings and children otherwise stateless, modes A03a and A03b, aren't held by the form); by descent from either parent, with no further limit on a child born abroad. Changes to the law at birth after 1 January 2024 weren't checked for this file. On 2026-11-03 the primary was read: Ministry of Interior, Egypt (الإدارة العامة للجوازات والهجرة والجنسية), e-services portal, nationality section description. It confirmed loss on taking another citizenship and descent. It was silent on the years of residence, renunciation and birth in the territory, which still rest on the sources above, re-read that day and found the same.
